equations.title: Connection Scan, backward (latest departure) recurrence
equations.latex: \begin{aligned} &LA[s] \leftarrow \tau - \mathrm{walk}(s \to D)\ \ \text{(stops near } D),\qquad LV, LA \leftarrow -\infty\ \text{elsewhere}\\ &\text{for } c = (u \to x,\ d_c, a_c, \mathrm{trip}_c) \text{ by decreasing } d_c \text{ with } a_c \le \tau:\\ &\quad \mathrm{ok}[\mathrm{trip}_c] \mathrel{|}= \left(a_c \le LA[x]\right);\ \ \text{if } \mathrm{ok}[\mathrm{trip}_c]:\ LV[u] \leftarrow \max(LV[u], d_c),\ \ LA[u] \leftarrow \max(LA[u], LV[u] - \mathrm{xfer}_u),\\ &\qquad LA[w] \leftarrow \max(LA[w], LV[u] - \mathrm{fp}(w \to u))\ \ \forall w \to u\\ &\mathrm{depart}(O) = \max_{s \text{ near } O}\ \left(LV[s] - \mathrm{walk}(O \to s)\right) \end{aligned}
equations.meaning: LV[s] = latest time one can board at stop s and still reach destination D by deadline tau; LA[s] = latest vehicle arrival at s that still works. Footpaths (<= 300 m) are relaxed only from vehicle labels (no chained walks); pickup/drop-off flags are respected. One scan per campus building x day type x 5-min slot (06:00-26:30) is precomputed, so every listing is answered from the same labels. The trip is then compared with walking (and biking if allowed): arrive-by returns the latest-leaving option, each transfer counted as 2 min.

limitations: Transit times come from a representative service week of the fall-2026 GTFS feeds (UM Blue Bus + AAATA TheRide), not real-time data; holidays, detours and special schedules are not modelled.
No bus delays or ride-time variability (no AVL data): a fixed 5-minute arrival buffer stands in for reliability.
Observed listing prices come from search-result text (verification 'search_extract'), not verified listing pages; prices, fees and availability can differ from the landlord's current offer.
Utility amounts are model estimates (heating intensity bands, default square footage, typical prices), shown as bands; they are not bills.
Value of time (50% of wage, $15/h default wage) and the late-night cost ($0.10 per outdoor minute) are assumptions; the breakeven panel shows where they would change the answer.
Co-op work hours are assumed (4 h/wk, range 3-6) when a listing does not state them, and meals are offset with an assumed $250/mo grocery spend.
Synthetic listings (ids starting with syn-) are fictional examples, labeled 'synthetic' everywhere they appear.
The roommate split is envy-free for the stated room values but not strategy-proof: members could misreport values (Dufton & Larson 2011).

The AI schedule/listing parsers were evaluated on a small synthetic set (18 + 6 held-out schedules, 8 + 3 listing texts; ledger/ai/EVAL.md), so scores are noisy; every parsed event is shown with its source quote to confirm.
The weekly routine is assumed to hold every week of the month (4.348 weeks); breaks and exam weeks are not discounted, and Monte Carlo does not re-optimise day tours per draw.

sections.title: Lease Ledger decision engine (`ledger/engine/`)
sections.summary: The engine turns a student's week and a set of listings into one dollar-denominated monthly ledger per home. It then reports how sure that answer is, what would flip it, and why an input change moved it. Everything is deterministic: seeded Monte Carlo, sorted tie-breaks and template-generated explanation sentences. Every number in a sentence is read from a computed field.

sections.title: Judge one-minute explanation
sections.summary: > We price your **actual week**, not a distance. For every candidate home we chain your classes into day tours: home to first event, event to event (or home in between only when that is cheaper), last event to home. Each trip comes from the bus timetable. Riding minutes count 1x. Walking and waiting count 1.75x (Wardman; Small & Verhoef), more on snowy days (NOAA: 21 of 31 January days have snow cover). Minutes the timetable forces you to arrive early count 0.5x (Small's schedule delay). Hours b

sections.title: Public API (`facade.py`, exported from `ledger.engine`)
sections.summary: `load_params()`, `evaluate`, `robustness`, `counterfactual`, `compare`, `diff`, `group`. The signatures and return shapes are listed in the module docstrings. `EvaluationResult.manifest` carries `provider.manifest()`, every parameter used (value, low, high, provenance, source, note), the weighted-criteria view, the Pareto front and the baseline method.

sections.title: Equations (units in brackets; module in parentheses)
sections.summary: `Profile.home_return`: "auto" picks the cheaper plan, "never" always goes direct, and "always" goes home whenever that is feasible. The engine warns about overlaps and late arrivals. Back-to-back transitions (one event ends exactly when the next starts elsewhere) are aggregated into a single warning and counted in `extras`. Provider calls and whole day tours are memoised per provider instance. If the provider has a batch method `arrive_by_many`, home-to-first-event queries are prefetched with it
equations: **Value of time (valuation.py).** `v = Profile.value_of_time` (provenance user), else `v = f × wage`, with f = 0.5 [-] (USDOT 2016 revised VTTS guidance for personal local travel, range 0.35 to 0.6) and wage = `Profile.hourly_wage` or a default of $15/h. With these defaults v = $7.50/h. The uncertainty range is `Profile.value_of_time_range`, or [0.5v, 2v] when none is given.

**Weather (valuation.py).** `P_bad(m) = snow_cover_days(m) / days(m)` comes from NOAA 1991–2020 normals, station USC00200230, MLY-SNWD-AVGNDS-GE001WI. `w(M) = 1 + winter_aversion × (b − 1) × mean_{m∈M} P_bad(m)`, with b = 1.3 for a bad day. This is the expected multiplier over days: a bad day counts b, a normal day counts 1. M is `{Profile.month}` if that is set, otherwise the season's months (fall = Sep–Nov, winter = Dec–Mar, spring = Apr–Aug).

**Trip components (valuation.py).** For each trip: `stationary = total − walk − ivt − bike` [min]. For an arrive-by transit trip, `early = max(0, deadline − (end of last bus leg + walking after it))` and `wait = max(0, stationary − early)`. Headway rule: if the first boarding's headway is h ≤ 10 min (taken from `Trip.note` "headway=NN", or from the provider's `headway` attribute), then wait = h/2 and early = 0, because the student arrives at the stop at random. Otherwise the student times their departure and the slack counts as schedule delay.
**Generalized minutes:** `G = ivt·1 + (walk·1.75 + wait·1.75 + bike·1.0)·w(M) + transfers·10 + early·0.5` [in-vehicle-equivalent min]. Weekly G is the sum over every trip of every day tour.
- `therms = HDD(M) × I(class) × sqft/1000`, where I is in therms/HDD/1000 sqft by building type and age band. An unknown year spans all house bands.
- `parking` = home spot + UM permit / 12, applied only if `needs_parking`.
- `insurance` is added. `transport = fare × bus trips × wpm = 0`, because the Blue Bus is free and TheRide is free with an MCard (MRide).

- `food_offset` = −$250 (assumed, $200–350) when `board_included`, so that co-op meal plans compare against rent plus groceries. `member_labor = v × h × 4.348`, where h is `Listing.member_labor_hours_week`, or 4 h/wk (assumed, 3–6) for co-ops. It is a time cost, not cash, and it is included in all_in.
- `time_value = v × G/60 × 4.348`.
- `late_night = $0.10/min × late_night_weight × outdoor minutes after 22:00 × 4.348`.
- `amenity_gap = $40 × Σ importance × (1 − has)`.
- `cash` = rent + fees + utilities + parking + insurance + transport + food. `all_in = cash + time_value + late_night + member_labor`. **score = all_in + amenity_gap**, lower is better.

**Scoring (scoring.py).** Hard constraints are rent_cap (rent only), all_in_cap (cash), bedrooms_min, household fit, max_single_trip_min, excluded_building_types, pets and parking. The money-metric rank applies to the feasible set. The secondary weighted view is `s_i = Σ_j w_j x_ij / median_feasible(x_j)` over (cash, time, late, 1 − fit). Median normalization is used instead of min–max to limit rank reversal. A home is on the Pareto front if no other feasible home is ≤ on all four criteria and < on one. The **portal baseline** keeps listings with rent ≤ cap and sorts them by straight-line distance to the single most frequent destination; it shows what the week-aware model adds.

**Infeasibility (infeasible.py).** `eliminated[c]` counts the listings that violate c. The binding constraint is argmax_c of the number of listings whose only violation is c. Minimal relaxation is the min required value (for caps) or the max required value (for bedrooms and household) over those listings. `restores[c]` = listings made feasible by changing only c to its minimal relaxation (for a non-numeric c, by dropping it). Hand-checked ledgers: `WORKED_EXAMPLES.md` (`python3 analysis/tools/worked_examples.py`).
- `score = K + v·T`, with T = (G/60 + co-op work h) × wpm, so `v* = (K_b − K_a)/(T_a − T_b)`.
- `score = K' + m·U`, with m a common multiplier on all utility prices, so `m* = (K'_b − K'_a)/(U_a − U_b)`.
- `rent_b* = rent_b + score_a − score_b`.
- Weight LP: `min ‖δ‖₁` s.t. `(w+δ)·(z_b − z_a) ≤ −ε`, `w+δ ≥ 0`, `Σδ = 0`, solved with HiGHS.

The engine uses common random numbers. Generalized minutes are linear in the components, so `G[s,l] = C[k_s,l]·m_s`, where C is the 6-vector of weekly components computed once per distinct schedule. Cost is then O(S·L) numpy arithmetic: about 0.2 s for S = 2000 and 60 listings. Outputs are P(rank 1), rank P10/50/90, score P10/50/90, `SE = max_l √(p(1−p)/S)`, and drivers: one-factor-at-a-time flip rates over S/4 draws.

**Diff (diff.py).** The engine runs an intermediate case M (the *after* schedule with the *before* parameters), so that `Δ = (M − before)` [schedule effect] `+ (after − M)` [other inputs], exactly. The schedule effect is explained trip by trip: day, from and to, query, mode, route, departure time and minutes, before vs after. Rank changes and the overtaking decomposition are reported as well.
- `W_pr = V_pr − c_p`, where c_p is member p's own travel cost from this home. V_pr is either given, or derived as cap + $75 for a private bath + $1/sqft/mo relative to the mean room (assumed).

- Maximin LP (Gal, Mash, Procaccia & Zick, "Which is the fairest (rent division) of them all?", EC 2016 / JACM 2017): `max u` s.t. `W_pσp − π_σp ≥ u` and `W_pσp − π_σp ≥ W_pσq − π_σq`, with `Σπ = R` and optional `π_σp ≤ cap_p`.

**Trip components (valuation.py).** For each trip: `stationary = total − walk − ivt − bike` [min]. For an arrive-by transit trip, `early = max(0, deadline − (end of last bus leg + walking after it))` and `wait = max(0, stationary − early)`. Headway rule: if the first boarding's headway is h ≤ 10 min (taken from `Trip.note` "headway=NN", or from the provider's `headway` attribute), then wait = h/2 and early = 0, because the student arrives at the stop at random. Otherwise the student times their departure and the slack counts as schedule delay.
**Generalized minutes:** `G = ivt·1 + (walk·1.75 + wait·1.75 + bike·1.0)·w(M) + transfers·10 + early·0.5` [in-vehicle-equivalent min]. Weekly G is the sum over every trip of every day tour.
- `therms = HDD(M) × I(class) × sqft/1000`, where I is in therms/HDD/1000 sqft by building type and age band. An unknown year spans all house bands.
- `parking` = home spot + UM permit / 12, applied only if `needs_parking`.
- `insurance` is added. `transport = fare × bus trips × wpm = 0`, because the Blue Bus is free and TheRide is free with an MCard (MRide).

- `food_offset` = −$250 (assumed, $200–350) when `board_included`, so that co-op meal plans compare against rent plus groceries. `member_labor = v × h × 4.348`, where h is `Listing.member_labor_hours_week`, or 4 h/wk (assumed, 3–6) for co-ops. It is a time cost, not cash, and it is included in all_in.
- `time_value = v × G/60 × 4.348`.
- `late_night = $0.10/min × late_night_weight × outdoor minutes after 22:00 × 4.348`.
- `amenity_gap = $40 × Σ importance × (1 − has)`.
- `cash` = rent + fees + utilities + parking + insurance + transport + food. `all_in = cash + time_value + late_night + member_labor`. **score = all_in + amenity_gap**, lower is better.

**Scoring (scoring.py).** Hard constraints are rent_cap (rent only), all_in_cap (cash), bedrooms_min, household fit, max_single_trip_min, excluded_building_types, pets and parking. The money-metric rank applies to the feasible set. The secondary weighted view is `s_i = Σ_j w_j x_ij / median_feasible(x_j)` over (cash, time, late, 1 − fit). Median normalization is used instead of min–max to limit rank reversal. A home is on the Pareto front if no other feasible home is ≤ on all four criteria and < on one. The **portal baseline** keeps listings with rent ≤ cap and sorts them by straight-line distance to the single most frequent destination; it shows what the week-aware model adds.

**Infeasibility (infeasible.py).** `eliminated[c]` counts the listings that violate c. The binding constraint is argmax_c of the number of listings whose only violation is c. Minimal relaxation is the min required value (for caps) or the max required value (for bedrooms and household) over those listings. `restores[c]` = listings made feasible by changing only c to its minimal relaxation (for a non-numeric c, by dropping it). Hand-checked ledgers: `WORKED_EXAMPLES.md` (`python3 analysis/tools/worked_examples.py`).
- `score = K + v·T`, with T = (G/60 + co-op work h) × wpm, so `v* = (K_b − K_a)/(T_a − T_b)`.
- `score = K' + m·U`, with m a common multiplier on all utility prices, so `m* = (K'_b − K'_a)/(U_a − U_b)`.
- `rent_b* = rent_b + score_a − score_b`.
- Weight LP: `min ‖δ‖₁` s.t. `(w+δ)·(z_b − z_a) ≤ −ε`, `w+δ ≥ 0`, `Σδ = 0`, solved with HiGHS.

The engine uses common random numbers. Generalized minutes are linear in the components, so `G[s,l] = C[k_s,l]·m_s`, where C is the 6-vector of weekly components computed once per distinct schedule. Cost is then O(S·L) numpy arithmetic: about 0.2 s for S = 2000 and 60 listings. Outputs are P(rank 1), rank P10/50/90, score P10/50/90, `SE = max_l √(p(1−p)/S)`, and drivers: one-factor-at-a-time flip rates over S/4 draws.

**Diff (diff.py).** The engine runs an intermediate case M (the *after* schedule with the *before* parameters), so that `Δ = (M − before)` [schedule effect] `+ (after − M)` [other inputs], exactly. The schedule effect is explained trip by trip: day, from and to, query, mode, route, departure time and minutes, before vs after. Rank changes and the overtaking decomposition are reported as well.
- `W_pr = V_pr − c_p`, where c_p is member p's own travel cost from this home. V_pr is either given, or derived as cap + $75 for a private bath + $1/sqft/mo relative to the mean room (assumed).

- Maximin LP (Gal, Mash, Procaccia & Zick, "Which is the fairest (rent division) of them all?", EC 2016 / JACM 2017): `max u` s.t. `W_pσp − π_σp ≥ u` and `W_pσp − π_σp ≥ W_pσq − π_σq`, with `Σπ = R` and optional `π_σp ≤ cap_p`.

fraction_of_wage.source: USDOT Office of the Secretary, Departmental Guidance on Valuation of Travel Time in Economic Analysis (1997; Rev.1 2003; Rev.2 2016): local personal travel = 50% of hourly income, plausible range 35-60%
fraction_of_wage.note: Government guidance value (not a student-specific estimate). 'observed' = taken verbatim from published guidance. 2016 PDF host blocked this session; 50% and the 35-60% band confirmed via search extracts of the guidance series.

default_student_wage_usd_h.source: U-M Student Employment Office: $15/h floor for all on-campus temporary and student positions since 2022-08-21 (SEO newsletter fall 2022); Michigan minimum wage $13.73 from 2026-01-01 (michigan.gov/leo), $15.00 from 2027-01-01; postings seen up to ~$18.75
default_student_wage_usd_h.note: Low = state minimum 2026; high = upper end of student postings seen (job-aggregator, weak). U-M floor not re-verified for AY2026-27.

default_vot_usd_h.source: Computed 0.5 x $15/h (USDOT share x U-M student wage floor). Range: 0.35 x $13.73 = $4.81 to 1.0 x $15 (full wage: student who would otherwise work). Student VOT studies span roughly EUR1.4-18/h (Trieste RP/SP) and $6-23/h (US SP studies)
default_vot_usd_h.note: Dominant input; the app should show hours first and let the user set VOT; Monte Carlo over [low, high].

in_vehicle.note: All other time components are expressed as in-vehicle-minute equivalents.

walk.source: Wardman et al. worldwide meta-analysis of time multipliers (2872 multipliers, 606 studies, 52 countries, 1963-2023; indexed TRID 2026): supports reducing the conventional 2.0 to 1.75 (RP emphasis) or 1.50 (SP emphasis). USDOT guidance: walk/wait/transfer at 100% of wage vs 50% for in-vehicle => 2.0. Abrantes & Wardman (2011) UK meta-analysis: walk/wait ratio 'substantially lower than two'.
walk.note: Applies to access/egress walks of transit trips and to pure-walk trips. Bad-weather adjustment applied on top (weather.bad_day_walk_multiplier).

wait.source: Same sources as walk (Wardman worldwide meta-analysis 1.5-1.75; USDOT 2.0; Abrantes & Wardman 2011 <2)
wait.note: Applies to time actually standing at the stop (incl. outdoor exposure). Forced early arrival at destination is NOT wait; use schedule_delay_early_per_min.

bike.source: No verified cycling-time multiplier found this session; set equal to in-vehicle time
bike.note: Exercise co-benefit vs effort/exposure roughly offset by assumption. Winter cycling handled by weather; consider disabling bike on snow-cover days.

transfer_penalty_min.source: Garcia-Martinez et al. (2018) Transp. Res. A 114:52-66, Madrid SP: pure transfer penalty = 15.2-17.7 in-vehicle minutes (excluding walk/wait). Currie (2005) J. Public Transp. 8(1): review avg bus-bus transfer penalty ~22 min (range 5-50), not netting out walk/wait
transfer_penalty_min.note: Added per transfer, in in-vehicle minutes, on top of the transfer walk and wait already charged at walk/wait multipliers. Scaled below Madrid metro commuters' value because campus trips are short and UM/AAATA transfers are mostly same-stop or short walks; this scaling is our assumption.

schedule_delay_early_per_min.source: Small (1982) AER 72(3):467-479 scheduling model; Small's own bottleneck review summarizes his estimates as approx beta/alpha = 0.5 (early) and gamma/alpha = 2 (late). Wardman, Chintakayala & de Jong (2016) Transp. Res. A 94:93-111 also meta-analyse schedule-delay-early/late values
schedule_delay_early_per_min.note: DIMENSIONLESS multiplier on VOT: each minute of forced early arrival beyond arrival_buffer_min costs 0.5 x VOT/60 dollars. Early time on campus is partly usable (study), hence < in-vehicle.

bad_day_walk_multiplier.source: Physical slowdown: Fossum (winter pavement, Norway) ~+1 min/km on best winter surface, ~+2 min/km on clean ice vs bare pavement (~+8-17% at 12 min/km); computer-vision study in a cold region: speed -0.102 m/s on snow cover (~-8% at 1.3 m/s). Discomfort: 2026 preprint DCE finds per-minute WTP for time savings rises ~1.66x in rain vs sun (rain, not snow; unreviewed)
bad_day_walk_multiplier.note: A 'bad day' = day with snow depth >= 1 in (NOAA SNWD normals). Multiplies walk and outdoor wait minutes on those days; expected monthly factor = 1 + (m-1) * snow_cover_days/days_in_month * Profile.winter_aversion. Value combines ~10-15% slower walking with a modest discomfort premium; not a single-study estimate.

usd_per_outdoor_min.source: No study found that prices walking after dark in $/min. Context: Gallup (2023 release) 40% of US adults afraid to walk alone at night within a mile of home; women 53% vs men 26%. Lighting/reassurance literature (Fotios et al.) shows route avoidance after dark but no time-equivalent
usd_per_outdoor_min.note: Extra $ per outdoor minute (walking or waiting) after 22:00, scaled by Profile.late_night_weight. $0.10/min = $6/h, i.e. ~+45% on a walk minute at default VOT ($7.50 x 1.75 = $13.1/h). Wide range on purpose; show it as a user slider.

home_return_min_gap.source: Project day-tour rule (concepts/final-recommendation.md v2): go home between events only if gap > round trip + this slack
home_return_min_gap.note: Minutes of at-home time needed to make a trip home worthwhile. Kobus et al. (2015) show long-commute students visit campus fewer days but stay longer: consistent with chaining.

arrival_buffer_min.source: Project rule (final-recommendation.md v2). Theory: with schedule-delay costs beta (early) and gamma (late), the cost-minimizing on-time probability is gamma/(beta+gamma) ~= 2/(0.5+2) = 0.8 (Small 1982; Noland & Small 1995)
arrival_buffer_min.note: Deterministic buffer used with GTFS times. If ride-time noise is modeled, replace by the 80th-percentile travel time (see literature-review.md, upgrade U4).

academic_weeks_per_year.source: U-M Board of Regents, proposed Ann Arbor calendar 2026-27 (regents.umich.edu meeting 09-2025, via search extract): fall classes begin Mon 2026-08-31; 69 class days in fall and 69 in winter. 69/5 = 13.8 class weeks + ~1 week of exams/study days per term

value_of_time_derivation: Your time is valued at $8.00/h = 50% x $16.00/h your wage (USDOT convention: personal local travel at 50% of hourly income).

Weather (Jan): 67% of days have snow cover (NOAA 1991-2020 normals), each counting outdoor minutes at 1.3x, scaled by your winter aversion 1 => outdoor-minute multiplier x1.202.

warnings: Template 'Music / Art & Design (North Campus)' adds 4 typical events (first alternative per slot; the robustness view samples the alternatives); 3 skipped because they overlap your own events.

value_of_time_derivation: Your time is valued at $8.00/h = 50% x $16.00/h your wage (USDOT convention: personal local travel at 50% of hourly income).

Weather (Jan): 67% of days have snow cover (NOAA 1991-2020 normals), each counting outdoor minutes at 1.3x, scaled by your winter aversion 1 => outdoor-minute multiplier x1.202.
warnings: Template 'Engineering sophomore/junior (mostly North Campus)' adds 5 typical events (first alternative per slot; the robustness view samples the alternatives); 3 skipped because they overlap your own events.
